transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, Doc, it’s a bit of a story, to be honest. I mean, I’ve been driving a truck for going on thirty years now, right? Started right out of high school. And you know, out on the road, you gotta be sharp. You gotta keep your eyes on the road, your mind on the schedule, the weigh stations, the logs—all of it. But lately... well, what finally got me in here is that over these last few months, my mind just keeps jumping all over the place. I’ll be cruising down I-80, and suddenly every little chirp on the CB radio, every single fuel price sign at the truck stops, every billboard... it just grabs me. And not just that, but I get these new ideas, like, completely new business ideas or ways to route things, just flooding in. And because my brain is bouncing around like a pinball, I’m missing details I normally never, ever miss. I mean, I’m the guy who always checks everything twice, but recently? I’ve missed a client’s delivery note, which caused a whole big mess at the dock, and I’ve completely forgotten who I promised to call back for dispatch. It’s like I can’t filter anything out anymore, and it’s just exhausting trying to keep my head straight when everything around me feels like it’s screaming for my attention.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually elevated, such as feeling overly confident, irritable, or not needing as much sleep lately?

Well, now that you mention it... yeah, I guess you could say that. It’s been going on for months now, actually. It’s like I’m running hot, you know? Sometimes I get this feeling—like I’m just completely fired up. I’ll be sitting in the cab, looking out over the highway, and I just get this overwhelming sense that everything is going to work out perfectly, no matter what happens. Like I’m on top of the world and nothing can touch me. I even started telling my dispatcher that we should double our routes, that I could handle it all, no sweat. Which, looking back, is pretty crazy because I’m already spread thin. 

But then, on the flip side of that... I’ve been getting really, really snappy. And I mean over the littlest things. Like, I’ll be home for the weekend, trying to relax, and my wife will just ask me a simple question about dinner, or maybe I’m out in the yard trying to fix the lawnmower, and if one bolt won’t turn right, I just lose it. I mean, I’m snapping at her, I’m throwing wrenches... it’s just not my usual way. I’m usually a pretty easygoing guy, you know? I’ve always been the one to keep my cool, especially with the family, but lately, it’s like my fuse is just a quarter-inch long. And it’s not just at home, either. I’ve caught myself getting furious at other drivers for things I’d normally just brush off. It’s like I’m either flying high and thinking I can conquer the world, or I’m just totally irritated by everything breathing around me. So, yeah, I guess my mood has been pretty out of whack.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of elevated mood, increased energy, racing thoughts, impulsivity, and irritability are consistent with bipolar I disorder, current episode manic without psychotic features. Other candidates such as ADHD (F90.0), schizoaffective disorder (F20.3), and unspecified mood disorders (F06.1, F06.2, F06.9) are ruled out based on the clear episodic pattern and presence of full manic episodes. Bipolar I is favored over bipolar II (F31.0) due to the presence of full manic episodes rather than hypomanic episodes.
